idiom_name: Pekko typed Behaviors as FSM + Pekko Persistence (event-sourced state)
implementation_notes: Pekko (the Akka 2.6 fork) supplies the whole role structure: one stateful actor per process instance, states and transitions expressed as typed behaviors (Behaviors.withTimers for deadlines, onTimeout for idle expiry), and Pekko Persistence making the instance durable by replaying persisted events rather than storing a snapshot. Messages to the instance are the triggers and replies, and the mailbox serialises them, so the correlation between an instance and its messages falls out of the actor id instead of a lookup table. Choose it when the runtime is already actor-based; in plain Scala a sealed-trait state machine plus an explicit row is leaner and easier to test.
pitfalls: Event sourcing replays events on recovery: any side effect performed directly in the command handler (outside Effect.persist/thenRun) is repeated or lost, and the replay must be deterministic.
State timeouts are one-shot for the current behavior: after a transition the deadline has to be re-armed, or the instance waits forever with no timeout.
Persistence ids must be unique per instance; reusing an id across different flows replays unrelated events into the wrong manager.
Stash is bounded and its order after unstashAll is not a transaction: replies stashed during recovery can be processed before the state they expect.
